solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Key cut separates each overturned piece of meat

parts.note: ESC is the escape key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: the cut word comes between the two letters of the turned-round abbreviation, separating them
overturned in a down-to-up sense means the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A cook slices through every upturned piece of meat with a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is the computer escape key, not a lock; 'overturned' and 'separates' work on the abbreviation for each, putting the cut inside its turned letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin boneless slice of veal or other meat, beaten flat.

clue.text: Maybe wind left Yankee exiting festival

indicators.note: the left and Yankee letters are leaving the wind word

parts.note: an easterly is one kind of wind, hence maybe
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A windy festival where a left-wing American walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exiting' takes L and Y off the end of EASTERLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian spring festival celebrating the Resurrection.

clue.text: Changeable person smoked joint in church somewhere in Spain

indicators.note: the joint goes in the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a ham is a cured, often smoked, joint of meat
Leon is a city and region of northern Spain

explanation.surface: A fickle type smokes a joint inside a Spanish church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoked joint' suggests cannabis but means cured meat; 'in' places it within the Church of England abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon is a lizard that changes colour, so figuratively someone who keeps shifting views.

clue.text: Authorised to go away on foot

definitions.meaning: slang for legitimate, lawful or approved
slang meaning to run off or flee on foot

explanation.surface: Permission is given to leave by walking.
explanation.definitionFit: Legit is informal for lawful; leg it is British slang for running away.

clue.text: Unit of troops having half a lager in pub number ten

indicators.note: the half-measure sits in the pub-number-ten letters

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: half means the first three letters of the six in a lager

explanation.surface: Troops having half a lager at a pub called Number Ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the first half of the two words 'a lager' together; 'in' sets that between the pub abbreviation and N plus X.
explanation.definitionFit: A phalanx was a tightly massed body of infantry in ancient Greek warfare.

clue.text: Postpone retiring high-spirited bigwig

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for high-spirited is read backwards

parts.note: someone up is in high spirits
a toff is a posh, important-seeming person

explanation.surface: A cheerful grandee who is retiring decides to delay things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns only the high-spirited word round. A toff is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off a meeting is to delay or defer it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Draw sun flickering over endless evergreen shrubland

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the sun letters come above the shrub
flickering suggests unsteady movement, so the letters of sun are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endless means the shrub word loses its final letter

parts.note: heather is an evergreen shrub covering moorland

explanation.surface: Painting a flickering sun over evergreen moorland that seems endless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flickering' turns SUN into UNS; 'endless' cuts HEATHER to HEATHE. 'Draw' looks artistic but means pull out a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a sword is to pull it from its scabbard, freeing the blade.

clue.text: Brownish-yellow Scandinavian coin found around clubhouse

indicators.note: the coin word goes around the clubhouse letters

parts.note: the ore is a small coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway
CH is the abbreviation for clubhouse

explanation.surface: A yellowish Nordic coin is found near the clubhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment, a dull yellowish-brown colour.

clue.text: Perhaps one over six feet ten keeps reversing car with strain ultimately

indicators.note: the feet-ten letters hold the turned car inside them
reversing means the word car is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
ten written as the digits one and zero looks like IO

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of strain

explanation.surface: A man over six feet keeps reversing a car under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' gives RAC, 'keeps' puts it between F and TIO, and 'ultimately' adds N. 'One over six' is a sixth.
explanation.definitionFit: One sixth, written as one above six, is an example of a fraction.

clue.text: Quiet husband enters building again somewhere in south-east Asia

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet

indicators.note: the husband letter goes into the rearranged letters, entering them
the letters of the word again are being built up into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A quiet man is building again somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges the letters of again to ANGAI, and 'enters' puts the husband letter inside, giving ANGHAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghai is a vast Chinese port city on the eastern coast of Asia.

clue.text: Ask the man to drop every last complaint

indicators.note: every word of the phrase loses its final letter, dropping the last of each

explanation.surface: Someone is told to ask a man to give up every last thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop every last' removes K, E and N, the last letters of ASK, THE and MAN, leaving AS TH MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint here means an illness or ailment, and asthma is a chronic breathing disorder.

clue.text: Sport which is played on board, jack replacing learner

indicators.note: the jack letter takes the place of the learner letter

parts.note: ludo is a children's board game played with dice and counters
L is the learner sign on a British car
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

explanation.surface: A sport played on a board with a jack instead of a learner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps L in LUDO for J.
explanation.definitionFit: Judo is a Japanese martial art practised as a competitive combat sport.

clue.text: Standing before court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone is standing before a court of law.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing upright and straight-backed, rather than lying or sitting, is the adjectival sense here.

clue.text: Funny character encountered around noon, after morning exercise

indicators.note: the met-around-noon piece comes after the morning and exercise pieces

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning
to exercise a right is to use it

indicators.note: the word for encountered goes round the noon letter

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: A comic figure is met around midday after a morning workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny character' reads as a comedian but means the quality of being funny; 'around' and 'after' do the assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: A funny character of a situation is its comic quality, the mirth or fun it gives.

clue.text: Explosive stuff — helmet regularly needed when it's around

indicators.note: the word for it goes around the picked letters

parts.note: in crosswords 'it' commonly stands for sex or sex appeal

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of helmet, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A helmet is regularly needed when explosives are around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of helmet, and 'around' wraps the word for 'it' round them; 'it' as sex appeal is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Semtex is a plastic explosive notoriously used in terrorist bombings.

clue.text: One supposedly forecasts carrot to develop during Whit?

indicators.note: the rearranged carrot goes inside the word for whit

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as is a tad

indicators.note: to develop is to change form, so the letters of carrot are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fortune card foretelling a carrot will grow at Whitsun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to develop' rearranges carrot into ROTCAR, and 'during' places it inside. Whit looks like Whitsun, the Christian festival, but means a jot.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune-tellers lay out these cards claiming they predict what lies ahead.

clue.text: Active period without Mike, such as start of October

indicators.note: without means the period word loses its Mike letter

parts.note: a month is a period of time
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
EG, exempli gratia, means for example or such as

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of October

explanation.surface: An active period, without Mike, such as early October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes M from MONTH to leave ONTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the go means being busy and constantly moving, an idiom for active.

clue.text: Cosmetic treatment of head's restricting the old, old women

indicators.note: the reworked letters close round the old word, restricting it
a treatment works the letters over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of heads
ye is an old form of the
OW is the abbreviation for old woman or old women

explanation.surface: A beauty treatment for the head restricts aged, elderly women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment of' rearranges the letters of head's into ESHAD, and 'restricting' closes it round the old word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshadow is a coloured make-up powder brushed on the eyelids.

clue.text: Obsessive self-interest, for example, East European uncovered

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters are stripped off

parts.note: a Romanian is from Romania in Eastern Europe

explanation.surface: Selfish obsession, for example, revealed in an Eastern European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' removes R and N from the ends of ROMANIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an extreme preoccupation with oneself and one's own importance.

clue.text: Military leader, age fifty, on first book

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the age and fifty pieces sit after the first book

parts.note: GEN is short for Genesis, the first book of the Bible
an era is an age
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An army leader of fifty is reading the first book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first book' is Genesis, the first book of the Bible; 'on' puts the age and fifty pieces after it in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A general is a senior army officer commanding large formations of troops.

clue.text: Move that's on ice, as latest United target primarily unknown

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of each of the three words

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A footballing move is on ice as United's latest target is unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on ice' suggests a deal put on hold, but describes a figure-skating jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A lutz is a figure-skating jump taken from the back outside edge of one skate.

clue.text: Parisian that hugs group with daughter, having waited in line

indicators.note: the French word wraps around the group's letters, hugging them

parts.note: que is French for that, as a Parisian would say it
EU is the European Union, a group of countries

explanation.surface: A Parisian who hugs her group and daughter after a wait in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugs' wraps the French word for 'that' round the European Union's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who queued stood in a line waiting for their turn.

clue.text: Type of street that's demolished at Xmas? It's cracking

definitions.text: Type of street that's demolished at Xmas
definitions.meaning: ... Street is a brand of boxed chocolates eaten up at Christmas
cracking means excellent, describing something of high standard

explanation.surface: A street torn down at Christmas is a cracking thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Quality Street is a British tin of wrapped chocolates traditionally devoured over Christmas; demolished means eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin of chocolates is wolfed at Christmas, and as an adjective the word means excellent.

clue.text: Describing certain nights as a celebrity?

definitions.meaning: clear nights full of visible stars
like a star, a famous person

explanation.surface: A description of nights out spent as a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear nights are full of stars, and a celebrity's manner can be called star-like.

clue.text: Fixed stake pulled over by horse, a volatile thing

indicators.note: by means the reversed stake sits beside the horse word

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

indicators.note: pulled over means turned over, so the stake word is read backwards

parts.note: an ante is the fixed stake put in before a poker hand is dealt

explanation.surface: A tethering stake gets pulled over by a skittish horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled over' turns ANTE into ETNA; 'volatile' puns on being explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Etna in Sicily is one of the world's most active volcanoes, liable to erupt.

clue.text: Faceless governor bypasses constant health problem

indicators.note: the shortened governor goes around the constant, passing by it on both sides
faceless means losing the front letter

parts.note: a ruler governs
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A faceless governor ignores a persistent health problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faceless' cuts RULER to ULER, and 'bypasses' puts it around C.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is an open sore on the skin or stomach lining, a medical complaint.

clue.text: Some chant a hymn backwards? It's nonsense

indicators.note: the hidden run is read from right to left
some of the phrase means its letters are found inside it

explanation.surface: Chanting a hymn backwards is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' finds TAHYM inside chanT A HYMn and 'backwards' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an old-fashioned way of saying rubbish or I don't believe it.

clue.text: Lounge's central heating low at first

indicators.note: at first means the cow sound goes before the heating letters

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow

explanation.surface: A lounge's central heating is turned low at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' and 'low' look like a room and a setting; they are a verb and a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to loiter or hang about idly, a verb like lounge.

clue.text: German runner, one who tends to pet barking

indicators.note: barking means calling out, so the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: a necker is someone given to necking, kissing and petting

explanation.surface: A German dog-walker who tends to pet a barking dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' signals a sound-alike. Runner means a river: the Neckar flows through Stuttgart and Heidelberg.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neckar is a river in south-west Germany, and rivers run, so runner is crossword shorthand.

clue.text: Lady's request for food perhaps causing mayhem

parts.note: Lady Di was Diana, Princess of Wales, so Lady's gives DI'S
an order is what diners ask for in a restaurant

explanation.surface: A lady's meal request causes chaos in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorder is chaos and confusion, which is what mayhem means.

clue.text: Wear down half of tyre in Lincoln

indicators.note: the half-tyre goes inside Lincoln's name

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president

indicators.note: half of means the first three letters of the six-letter word for tyre

parts.note: a radial is a radial-ply tyre

explanation.surface: Half of a tyre wears down in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English city but is the president, Abe; 'half of' takes the first half of a radial tyre, and 'in' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to scrape or rub away by friction, as roads erode tyres.

clue.text: Incidentally, this is where police cameras usually are

definitions.meaning: a phrase meaning in passing, used to change the subject

definitions.text: this is where police cameras usually are
definitions.meaning: speed cameras stand beside the road, next to the route

explanation.surface: An aside about where speed cameras are usually placed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces a passing remark; literally, cameras are mounted at the roadside.
